skill.name: using-superpowers
skill.description: Guides AI agents to check and invoke applicable skills before responding, then follow process and implementation skills in the correct order.
skill.summary: Establishes a consistent skill-selection workflow for every new task.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. Lines 20 through 40 contain a Graphviz DOT diagram in documentation, not executable Ruby or shell commands. No semantic security issue was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The matched content is a fenced Graphviz DOT diagram describing a workflow. It contains no Ruby backtick expression, shell command, or executable command invocation.

content.user_title: Apply Skills Before Starting Any Task
content.value_statement: Agents can miss useful workflows when they respond before checking available skills. This skill enforces an early skill check and defines an ordered usage process.
actual_capabilities: Directs the agent to check available skills before responding or asking clarifying questions.
Defines a workflow for invoking applicable skills and announcing their purpose.
Requires checklist items to become explicit tasks when a selected skill includes a checklist.
Prioritizes process skills before implementation skills.
Distinguishes rigid skills from flexible pattern skills.
limitations: Provides process guidance only and does not execute code or discover skills independently.
Depends on the host environment providing skill and task-management tools.
Does not resolve every priority conflict between similar skills.
Its mandatory checks can add overhead to simple requests.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Starts
use_cases.description: Ensure every request begins with a consistent check for relevant skills before any response.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Engineering Workflows
use_cases.description: Apply debugging or brainstorming processes before selecting implementation guidance for coding tasks.

use_cases.title: Organize Skill Catalogs
use_cases.description: Clarify how process and implementation skills should be selected and ordered during complex work.

prompt_templates.title: Check Before Answering
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the available skills for this request. Invoke every applicable skill before answering, then state which skill you are using and why.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request requiring a basic skill check

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bug Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: For this bug, check process skills first, then domain skills. Use any required checklist and create one task for each item.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify relevant brainstorming and implementation skills for this feature. Apply them in priority order before inspecting files or proposing changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Feature development with multiple skill types

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Complex Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this multi-stage request for process and implementation skills. Explain the sequence, convert all checklists into tasks, and follow each selected skill precisely.

output: The agent checks available skills before investigating.
The agent selects a debugging process before relevant implementation guidance.
The agent creates tasks from any required checklist.

output_examples.output: The agent checks brainstorming guidance first, then applies the relevant frontend implementation skill before editing files.

best_practices: Keep the available skill catalog current so checks use the latest instructions.
Apply process skills before implementation skills when both are relevant.
Convert every required checklist item into a visible task before execution.
anti_patterns: Responding or asking questions before checking whether a skill applies.
Using remembered skill instructions without reading the current version.
Skipping required process skills because a task appears simple.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It directs an agent to check and invoke relevant skills before responding to a request.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It contains procedural guidance and a Graphviz workflow diagram, not executable code.

faq.question: Which tools does it require?
faq.answer: It expects a skill invocation tool and a task-management tool when selected skills contain checklists.

faq.question: Does it choose a specific implementation skill?
faq.answer: It defines priority rules, but the available catalog and current task determine the selected skill.

faq.question: Can skill instructions be adapted?
faq.answer: Rigid skills should be followed exactly. Flexible skills allow their principles to be adapted to the task.

faq.question: When should this skill be used?
faq.answer: Its instructions apply at the start of each conversation, before responses, questions, or task actions.
